_note: Shop-floor guidance used by the advisor. Stage 1 entries: bare-PCB fabrication defects (general practice in line with IPC-A-600). Stage 2 entries: assembled-board solder and component defects (general practice in line with IPC-A-610). Severities follow common accept/reject practice; this is not a certified inspection standard, so check limits against your own process and acceptance class.

missing_hole.label: Missing hole
missing_hole.what: A drilled hole that should be present is absent.
causes: Drill bit broken or worn out during the run
Hole missing from the drill file or wrong tool assignment
Drilling step skipped or stopped early on part of the panel
actions: Compare the board with the drill drawing to confirm the hole is required
Check the drill machine log and the bit for breakage
Re-drill if the process allows, otherwise reject the board and check the rest of the panel

mouse_bite.label: Mouse bite
mouse_bite.what: Small bites or notches along the edge of a copper trace, reducing its width.
causes: Over-etching or uneven etch rate
Defects or dust on the photoresist or phototool during imaging
Poor resist adhesion at the trace edge
actions: Measure the remaining trace width against the minimum allowed width
Reject if the width reduction exceeds the acceptance limit
Check etchant concentration, speed and resist exposure

open_circuit.label: Open circuit
open_circuit.what: A copper trace is broken, so the connection is lost.
causes: Over-etching through a narrow part of the trace
Scratch or handling damage across the trace
Dust or a resist defect that blocked copper during imaging
actions: Confirm with a continuity test across the break
Reject the board unless a repair is permitted for this product class
Inspect the phototool and etch settings for the same location on other boards

short.label: Short circuit
short.what: Unwanted copper connects two conductors that should be isolated.
causes: Under-etching leaving a copper bridge
Resist residue or contamination on the artwork
Dust or copper particles during imaging or plating
actions: Confirm with an electrical isolation test between the two nets
Reject, or remove the bridge only if rework is allowed, then re-test
Check etch time and cleanliness of phototools and the imaging area

spur.label: Spur
spur.what: A small copper protrusion sticking out from the edge of a conductor.
causes: Dust or a defect on the phototool
Incomplete development or under-etching
Resist defects at the conductor edge
actions: Measure the spacing between the spur and the nearest conductor
Reject if spacing falls below the minimum clearance
Clean or replace the phototool and check developer and etch settings

spurious_copper.label: Spurious copper
spurious_copper.what: An isolated patch of copper left where there should be none.
causes: Incomplete etching in that area
Resist splash or defect protecting copper that should be removed
Contamination on the panel before etching
actions: Check whether the copper reduces clearance to nearby conductors
Reject or remove it if rework is allowed, then re-inspect
Review etch uniformity and panel cleaning before imaging

hole_breakout.label: Hole breakout
hole_breakout.what: The drilled hole is not centred in its pad, so the copper ring around it is broken.
causes: Drill registration error or misaligned tooling
Panel stretch or shrink between imaging and drilling
Layer-to-layer misregistration
actions: Measure the remaining annular ring against the minimum allowed
Reject if the breakout exceeds the acceptance limit
Check drill registration and tooling pins before the next panel

conductor_scratch.label: Conductor scratch
conductor_scratch.what: A scratch on a copper conductor from handling or transport.
causes: Boards stacked without separators
Rough handling or conveyor contact
Tools or fixtures touching the surface
actions: Check whether the scratch reduces trace width or cuts through the copper
Reject if conductor thickness or width is below the limit
Improve handling: gloves, separators, conveyor inspection

conductor_foreign_object.label: Foreign object on conductor
conductor_foreign_object.what: Debris such as dust, fibre or resist particles on a copper conductor.
causes: Dust or fibres in the work area
Resist or film particles not cleaned off
Contaminated handling surfaces
actions: Clean the area (air blow or approved solvent) and re-inspect
Reject if the object is embedded or conductive and cannot be removed
Check cleanliness of the line and handling area

base_material_foreign_object.label: Foreign object on base material
base_material_foreign_object.what: Debris or an inclusion on or in the laminate between conductors.
causes: Contaminated laminate from the supplier
Debris trapped during lamination or handling
Dust in the work area
actions: Check whether it is conductive or reduces spacing between conductors
Clean if it is on the surface; reject if it is embedded in the laminate
Inform incoming inspection if laminate contamination repeats

insufficient_solder.label: Insufficient solder
insufficient_solder.what: A solder joint has too little solder to form a proper fillet between the lead and the pad.
causes: Too little solder paste from a blocked stencil aperture
Poor wetting from oxidised or contaminated pads or leads
Reflow or wave temperature profile too short or too cool
actions: Add solder and flux to the joint and check the fillet
Rework by adding solder and flux to the joint
Clean or check the stencil aperture and the paste volume on the printer

excess_solder.label: Excess solder
excess_solder.what: A solder joint has too much solder, forming a large ball or a fillet that hides the lead outline.
causes: Too much solder paste from a thick stencil
Paste smeared during printing or placement
Hand soldering with too much solder wire
actions: Check the joint does not touch nearby pads, remove extra with wick
Remove extra solder with solder wick if the joint is out of limits
Check stencil thickness, aperture size and printer pressure

solder_bridge.label: Solder bridge
solder_bridge.what: Solder joins two pads or leads that should be separate, creating an unwanted short circuit.
causes: Too much solder paste between fine-pitch pads
Stencil misaligned with the pads
Component pressed too hard or placed off position
actions: Remove the bridge with flux and solder wick, then check for a short
Check the joint and neighbouring pins for a short with a multimeter after rework
Check stencil alignment and paste volume on fine-pitch parts

solder_void.label: Solder void
solder_void.what: Gas pockets or holes inside or on the surface of a solder joint.
causes: Flux or moisture outgassing during reflow
Reflow profile with too short a soak or too fast a ramp
Contaminated pads or old solder paste
actions: Check the void size against the limit and rework large voids
Rework the joint if the void is large or on a power or thermal pad
Check paste age and storage, and adjust the reflow soak time

missing_component.label: Missing component
missing_component.what: A component that should be mounted on the board is absent from its pads.
causes: Pick-and-place nozzle failed to pick or dropped the part
Feeder empty or wrong part loaded
Part knocked off during handling or before reflow
actions: Confirm the position is populated in the BOM, then fit the part
Place and solder the missing part, then retest the board
Check the feeder and nozzle log on the pick-and-place machine

shifted_component.label: Shifted component
shifted_component.what: A component is displaced or rotated from its correct position on the pads.
causes: Placement offset in the machine program
Board vibration or knocks before reflow
Uneven pad heating causing the part to drift (tombstoning or skew)
actions: Check the lead overhang on the pads and realign the part
Reflow and realign the part, or replace it if it was damaged
Check placement offsets and the reflow profile

burn.label: Burn mark
burn.what: Discolouration or charring on the board or a component from overheating.
causes: Soldering iron held too long or too hot
Reflow temperature too high
Component overheating or electrical overstress in test
actions: Reject the board and check for lifted pads and damaged parts
Test the affected component and circuit before any rework
Check soldering iron temperature, reflow profile and test setup

physical_damage.label: Physical damage
physical_damage.what: A crack, chip, dent or broken part on a component or the board.
causes: Mechanical stress from handling or depaneling
Board flexing that cracks ceramic components
Dropped boards or tools striking the assembly
actions: Replace the cracked or chipped part and test the circuit
Test the circuit around the damaged part
Check handling, depaneling and fixture pressure on the line

oxidation.label: Oxidation
oxidation.what: Dull, discoloured or corroded copper or solder surfaces.
causes: Boards or parts stored too long in humid air
Missing or worn surface finish
Flux residues left on the board
actions: Clean the area and check that solder wets properly
Rework joints that do not wet properly
Check storage conditions, shelf life and cleaning after soldering
